title: Moon Position Map: Where the Moon Is Up Now
description: See where the Moon is above the horizon right now on the Moon Position Map — live sublunar point, moon-up region and phase. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, the region where the Moon is up at any moment covers about half the Earth, centred on the sublunar point — and that region slides roughly 50 minutes later each day, which is why last week's evening Moon is this week's midnight one.
quick_answer: The Moon Position Map shows where the Moon is above the horizon right now — the live moon-up hemisphere centred on the sublunar point, with the current phase. Click any place for its approximate moonrise and moonset: the lunar counterpart to the day-night map.
steps_intro: Half the planet has a Moon up. Is it yours?

body.t: Before stepping out: is the Moon even above your horizon, and how lit? One glance answers;
gives your street's exact times when the glance says maybe.
EME (Earth-Moon-Earth) operators need mutual visibility windows — the moon-up overlap between two stations is this map's two clicks.
Watch the moon-up region lag the Sun's day-night pattern by about 50 minutes daily and the lunar month stops being a list and becomes a mechanism.
A moonlit landmark needs the Moon up, lit and roughly behind the camera. The position map plus the phase narrows the world's candidate nights fast.

The point where the Moon stands overhead is always within about ±28.6° of latitude — the Moon's orbital tilt (5.1°) added to Earth's (23.4°). It can be overhead in Florida or Mumbai, never in London or Toronto.

At full moon the moon-up region centres on the midnight meridian — the Moon rises as the Sun sets, opposite the day-night map's lit half. A week later at last quarter, the Moon-up bulge sits over the dawn side instead.

faq: How far can the sublunar point wander?
Its latitude swings between about +28.6° and −28.6° across the 18.6-year nodal cycle; its longitude circles the Earth daily. The tropics own the overhead Moon; everyone else gets it at an angle.
Is the phase really identical worldwide?
At an instant, yes — one Sun-Moon geometry for the whole planet (the base questions cover this). What varies is the view's rotation: the lit edge tips differently by latitude and hour.
Why is the Moon sometimes up all day?

Near full it rules the night; near the quarters it shares the day — a first-quarter Moon rides the afternoon sky. 'Up' and 'visible' part company in daylight: position here, contrast decides the rest.
The map says up, but I cannot see it.
Haze, buildings, daylight glare or a thin crescent near the Sun can all hide a geometrically-up Moon. The map reports position, not visibility — the honest half it can compute.
How accurate are clicked rise and set estimates?
Approximate — sampled from the same truncated model. For planning an event around a moonrise, use the dedicated Moonrise and Moonset Calculator, which is built for the number.
Does the Moon-up region match the night region?

Only in passing. The two hemispheres drift through each other on the 29.5-day cycle: some nights the Moon-up half and the dark half coincide (glorious), some nights they are opposite (moonless dark — also glorious, to astronomers).
What is the Moon's path called?
It tracks near the ecliptic — the Sun's road, tilted 5.1° — which is why Moon and Sun meet at eclipses only when the Moon is near a node, and why this map and the day-night map rhyme.
